Uuid.description:
Opaque resource identifier. The pattern makes tsoa reject malformed IDs before they reach a
database query.

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name, or `null` when the user has no local login yet.

email.description: Email of the linked local login, or `null` when the user has no local login yet.

disabled.description: Disabled users cannot sign in, keep no sessions and lose TAK access.

passwordSet.description: `false` until the user has set a password; a setup link can then sign them in once.

accountEvent.description:
Set for event accounts, which are deleted when this event is archived; `null` for permanent
accounts.

userGroups.description: User groups the user belongs to, in the order they were added.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

UserAccountType.description: `permanent` accounts stay; `event` accounts are deleted when their event is archived.

url.description:
Single-use link for the user, returned exactly once. The token travels in the URL fragment,
which browsers never send to the server; the Web application exchanges it in a request body.

username.description:
Sign-in and TAK login name; derived from the display name when omitted. The person may still
change it while setting up the account.

email.description:
New email address, or `null` to remove it; only for users with a local login and with
`users.set-email`. It stays unverified until its owner confirms the link sent to it.

username.description:
New sign-in and TAK login name; only for users with a local login. Apps enrolled with the old
name keep working, because client certificates name the user ID.

eventId.description: Event the grant is limited to, or `null` for an instance-wide grant.

system.description:
Protected group managed by the server, such as the setup Admin group. It cannot be deleted,
its permissions cannot change and it always keeps at least one member.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

Slug.description: Lowercase ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens.

permissions.description: Complete replacement of the group's grants.

TakTrafficRecordingDto.description: Whether an event stores its TAK traffic, and for how long. Off by default.

retentionDays.description: Recorded positions and markers are deleted after this many days.

storedItems.description: Number of items currently stored for the event.

TakServerCertificateDto.description: The certificate the TAK listeners present. The private key is never returned.

source.description: OpenMeshTak-issued, administrator-added, obtained automatically through ACME, or read from the reverse proxy's files.

certificateFile.description: Full chain, server certificate first, e.g. `live/tak.example.org/fullchain.pem`.

enabled.description: Whether the TAK listeners run. Requires a host name.

hostName.description: Public host name or IPv4 address that ATAK and iTAK connect to.

clientCertificateDays.description: Lifetime of newly enrolled client certificates.

serverCertificate.description: `null` until the server first starts or a certificate is added.

certificateFiles.description: The reverse proxy's certificate files Core reads, relative to `certificateDirectory`; `null` unless used.

certificateDirectory.description: Where the proxy's certificate directory must be mounted for `certificateFiles`.

endpointChangedAt.description:
When the public host name or a port last changed after setup; `null` if never. Apps enrolled
before it may still use the old endpoint.

validClientCertificates.description:
Valid client certificates. Changing the host name or a port while this is above 0 requires
`endpointChange` in the update, because those apps must enroll again.

clientCertificatesToReEnroll.description:
Valid client certificates issued before `endpointChangedAt`; their apps may still point to the
old endpoint and must enroll again.

TakEndpointChangeConfirmation.description: The administrator's decision for a host name or port change that affects devices.

notifyAffectedUsers.description: Email users with enrolled apps that they must set them up again; otherwise only warn here.

endpointChange.description:
Required when this update moves a port to a non-standard value, or changes the host name or a
port while apps are enrolled. Core never changes a public port on its own.

certificateChainPem.description: Full chain in PEM format, server certificate first, e.g. the `fullchain.pem` of Let's Encrypt.

privateKeyPem.description:
Unencrypted private key in PEM format, e.g. the `privkey.pem` of Let's Encrypt. Encrypted at
rest and never returned.

UseTakCertificateFilesRequest.description: Use the reverse proxy's certificate files; both paths are relative to the mounted directory.

callsign.description: The app's callsign once it reported its position.

LiveTakItemDto.description: The newest state of one CoT item, such as a member's position or a marker they placed.

type.description: CoT type, e.g. `a-f-G-U-C` for a friendly ground unit.

LiveTakTrafficDto.description: Current TAK traffic of one event, held in memory only; nothing of it is stored.

TakEnrollmentDto.description:
Everything a TAK app needs to connect. Manual setup uses `username` with the account password;
the ATAK link and QR code carry a QR token instead, which is shown only in this response.

username.description: The account username, the TAK login name.

expiresAt.description:
When the QR token expires, from the token lifetime of the user's active events: a number of
days, or the event end. `null` when it does not expire (an event without end date) or when
`atakEnrollmentUrl` is `null`. Users without an active event get 30 days.

enrollmentPort.description: Public ports; they may differ from the listen ports inside the container.

martiPort.description: Public Marti port for Data Packages; the enrollment profile also sets it in ATAK.

atakEnrollmentUrl.description:
Link and QR code content for ATAK certificate enrollment, with the QR token. `null` while the
TAK server uses a certificate from its own CA, because ATAK's QR enrollment then fails.

itakQrString.description:
QR payload understood by iTAK's server scanner. It configures the SSL streaming endpoint and
iTAK then asks for the user's login. `null` with a private server certificate because the QR
cannot carry CA trust material.

itakPackageCertificateId.description:
The still valid certificate from an earlier iTAK package download. A new package is refused
until it is revoked, so each downloaded package stays one device.

TakClientCertificateDto.description: A client certificate issued to a TAK app. Certificates are public; no key material exists here.

clientUid.description: Device UID the app sent during enrollment, if any.

issuedForOldEndpoint.description:
Issued before the TAK server's host name or a port last changed; the app may still use the old
endpoint and must enroll again.

TakCertificateAuthorityDto.description: A TAK certificate authority. The certificate is public trust material; the key never leaves Core.

active.description: Signs new client and server certificates.

fingerprintSha256.description: SHA-256 of the DER certificate, lowercase hex, for comparing with what devices show.

certificatePem.description: The CA certificate in PEM format.

privateKeyPem.description:
The unencrypted CA private key in PEM format (PKCS#8 or PKCS#1). It is encrypted at rest and
never returned.

TakAcmeSettingsDto.description: ACME settings and renewal status. Provider tokens and the account key are never returned.

apiToken.description: Omit to keep the stored token, `null` to remove it. The token is encrypted and write-only.

TakAcmeTestResultDto.description: Result of a test run against Let's Encrypt staging.

message.description: What happened, safe to show to the administrator.

meshChannelId.description: Channel for the app's "TAK Mesh Channel"; `null` uses the primary channel.

configured.description: `false` until the first administrator exists; the Web app then opens the setup flow.

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens.

sequence.description: Increases by one per line since Core started; poll with the last one seen.

time.description: ISO 8601 time the line was written.

details.description: The remaining structured fields as JSON, already sanitized like the container log.

latestSequence.description: Pass as `after` on the next request to receive only newer lines.

reset.description: True when `items` starts a fresh view: no `after` was given or Core restarted since.

RegistrationMode.description:
Who may create their own account: nobody (`closed`, the default), people holding a
registration invite (`invite`), or anyone who can reach the instance (`open`).

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens.

inviteToken.description: Registration invite; required while registration is invite-only.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; `0` while the defaults were never saved.

inviteUrl.description:
Single-use registration link, returned exactly once. The token travels in the URL fragment,
which browsers never send to the server.

TakTeam.description:
ATAK team colors as listed by the upstream Meshtastic `atak.proto` `Team` enum, using the
display names ATAK writes into CoT `__group` elements. Verified 2026-10-04.

TakRole.description: ATAK member roles from the upstream Meshtastic `atak.proto` `MemberRole` enum.

ProfileTakServer.description: The built-in TAK server participants enroll with from the dashboard.

hostName.description: `null` while the TAK server is not enabled.

ProfileMeshtasticTakServer.description:
The Meshtastic app's local TAK server, which carries CoT over the mesh when there is no network.
`meshChannel` is the value for the app's "TAK Mesh Channel": the channel's slot on this member's
device, or `null` while that channel has not reached the device yet (then the primary channel
is used).

ProfileChannel.description:
A channel the member receives. `included` channels come with the member's channel set;
`on-site` channels are secret and handed out on site by a key holder before their release.

keyHolder.description: Holds this secret channel ahead of the event to share it on site.

ProfileFirmware.description: The Meshtastic firmware a participant must flash before importing OpenMeshTak settings.

recommendedVersion.description: As recommended by the event, e.g. `2.8` or `2.8.3`.

minimumVersion.description: Lowest version the settings are made for, e.g. `2.8.1`.

verified.description: `false` while no tested patch reaches the minimum version.

ResolvedProfileDto.description:
The single resolved provisioning identity of one member in one event. Every TAK, Meshtastic and
mission output is derived from this shape.

source.description:
`published` profiles use the event's latest configuration revision. `preview` profiles of
draft events use the current, unpublished configuration and are visible to administrators only.

meshtasticLocalServer.description: Meshtastic events also connect ATAK/iTAK to the Meshtastic app; `null` otherwise.

server.description: Every member enrolls with the built-in TAK server for Data Packages and CoT over the network.

serverGroups.description: The group's TAK server groups for an external TAK server; the built-in server ignores them.

firmware.description: `null` for configurations published before events had a firmware version.

channels.description: Device order, primary first. Channels outside the member's audience are absent.

shortName.description: `null` only in previews while the group has no short-name prefix.

meshtastic.description: `null` when the event does not use Meshtastic.

ChannelHandoutDto.description:
A secret-bearing Meshtastic channel handout. It is returned only to the signed-in key holder,
must not be persisted by clients and becomes obsolete as soon as the channel key rotates.

url.description: Canonical Meshtastic ChannelSet URL; the fragment contains the channel key.

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name of a user; `null` for API clients.

hasPassword.description: Whether a user can sign in with a password, which the TAK login needs; `false` for API clients.

permissions.description: Effective grants, deduplicated across all sources.

build.description: Short commit hash of the build, e.g. `8e6a88d`.

support.description:
`tested`: in a shipped profile's line and verified on a device; `supported`: in a shipped
profile's line at or above its minimum; `unsupported`: no shipped profile covers it.

profileId.description: The profile that covers the release, or null when it is unsupported.

status.description:
`current`: downloaded within the last 12 hours; `cached`: the last downloaded list, older than
12 hours because the flasher could not be reached or a refresh is underway; `unknown`: no list
has ever been downloaded; `disabled`: lookups are switched off.

fetchedAt.description: When the shown list was downloaded; null without a list.

releases.description: Full releases only, newest first; revoked and pull-request builds are left out.

checkEnabled.description: Look up published releases from the official Meshtastic flasher.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; 0 while the default is in use.

minVersion.description: Lowest supported patch of the line, e.g. `2.8.1`.

testedVersions.description: Patches verified on a real device. Newer patches are allowed but not verified.

since.description: First patch that has the field; hidden while the event's minimum version is lower.

managed.description: Resolved per member by OpenMeshTak and never editable.

secret.description: Write-only: set through the secrets endpoint and never returned. Has no default.

value.description: Upstream enum name stored in settings, e.g. `LONG_FAST`.

Record_string.FirmwareEnumValueDto-Array.description: Construct a type with a set of properties K of type T

minVersion.description: Lowest supported patch of the line, e.g. `2.8.1`.

testedVersions.description: Patches verified on a real device. Newer patches are allowed but not verified.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the profile file, recorded in configuration revisions.

enums.description: Allowed values per enum with English UI labels.

FirmwareSettingsDocument.description: Values of a firmware profile's editable fields, keyed by field key.

firmwareVersion.description: Recommended firmware: a line such as `2.8` or a minimum patch such as `2.8.3`.

effectiveMinimumVersion.description: The given patch or the profile minimum; `null` when the version is no longer supported.

verified.description: `false` when no tested patch reaches the effective minimum version.

secretFields.description: Secret fields available for the event's firmware version, set through `PUT secrets`.

secretsSet.description: Keys of secret fields that hold a value. The values themselves are never returned.

problems.description: Why the stored configuration is not valid for this Core release; empty when it is.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; 0 until the configuration is first saved.

settings.description: Complete or partial document; missing fields take the profile default.

SecretSettingsChanges.description: Values of write-only secret fields; `null` clears a value.

secrets.description: Only the secrets to change; others keep their value.

confirmation.description:
Token to send with the change when it needs confirmation; `null` when only the minimum patch
within the same line is raised, which never drops values.
The `confirmation` of the preview the administrator accepted.

ChannelPskKind.description:
How a channel encrypts traffic, derived from the PSK length as defined by upstream
`channel.proto`: no key disables encryption, one byte selects a well-known default key, and 16
or 32 bytes are AES-128 or AES-256 keys.

ChannelPskInfo.description: Describes the stored key without revealing it.

EventAudience.description:
A selection of event members: everyone who matches any listed group, role or member. Used by
Meshtastic channels and Data Packages so both decide "who receives this" the same way.

sortOrder.description: Channel order; the lowest value (oldest on ties) is the primary channel.

positionPrecision.description: Upstream position precision: 0 sends no position, 32 sends the full position.

secret.description:
Secret channels withhold their key from every participant view and artifact except those of
key holders until the channel is released.

releasedAt.description: When a secret channel was released to its whole audience; `null` while withheld.

keyHolders.description:
Members of the audience who receive a secret channel ahead of the event to share it on site.
Selected like the audience; only members who are also in the audience count.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

MeshtasticChannelName.description: Meshtastic channel name; ASCII so the upstream 11-byte limit equals the character count.

sortOrder.description: Defaults to after the last channel.

psk.description:
Optional base64 key: empty (no encryption), 1 byte (upstream default key), 16 or 32 bytes.
Omit it to let the server generate a random 32-byte key.

secret.description: Secret channels need an AES key. The primary channel may also be secret.
Turning a channel secret again withholds it until it is released anew.

psk.description: Optional replacement key in the same format as on creation; omit it for a random key.

RevealedChannelPsk.description: Plain key material; returned only by the audited reveal action.

psk.description: Base64 key exactly as Meshtastic clients expect it.

MemberDataPackageDto.description: A published Data Package a member receives, at its newest revision.

revision.description: Newest published revision; downloads always deliver this one.

installOnEnrollment.description: The built-in TAK server installs it in the app right after the app enrolls.

installOnConnection.description: The built-in TAK server installs it, and every new revision, whenever the app connects.

token.description: Single-use bearer value. Returned exactly once and never retrievable again.

claimUrl.description:
Link for the participant. The token travels in the URL fragment, which browsers never send
to the server; the Web application removes it from history before exchanging it.

MapSettingsDto.description: The Web map's online base map. Defaults to OpenStreetMap until an administrator changes it.

tileUrlTemplate.description: XYZ tile URL with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`; `{a-c}` selects subdomains.

attribution.description: Plain-text attribution the provider requires; the Web app shows it on every map.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; 0 while the default is in use.

InstanceSettingsDto.description: How this installation presents itself. Public, because the sign-in page shows it.

name.description: Shown as the browser page title, on the sign-in page and in account emails.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; 0 while the default is in use.

Core release version. Core and Web are released together: a Web app works with every Core of
the same major and minor version and warns otherwise.

memberCount.description: Members of the event, whatever their group or role.

openSyncIssueCount.description: Synchronized members that could not be resolved and wait for an administrator.

publishedRevision.description: Number of the configuration revision participants receive; `null` before the first one.

unpublishedChanges.description:
Whether an active event's current configuration differs from its published revision, so
participants do not see the changes until someone publishes. Always `false` for drafts
(activation publishes) and archived events (read-only).

EventListItemDto.description: An event in the overview list, with the facts organizers act on.

timeZone.description: IANA time-zone identifier used for event-local schedules, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

takLoginTokenDays.description:
Days a TAK login token (QR code or typed instead of the password) stays valid. `0` keeps it valid
until the event's end date, or with no end date it never expires. Tokens stop working anyway once the user
loses TAK access.

permanentAccounts.description:
Accounts created for this event (new members, synchronized participants) are permanent instead
of event accounts that are deleted when the event is archived.

meshtasticEnabled.description:
The event provisions Meshtastic radios. When off, profiles carry no Meshtastic part, radio
downloads are unavailable and channels and radio settings stay stored but unused. Like other
configuration it reaches participants of an active event with the next published revision.

timeZone.description: IANA time-zone identifier used for event-local schedules, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

takLoginTokenDays.description:
Days a TAK login token (QR code or typed instead of the password) stays valid. `0` keeps it valid
until the event's end date, or with no end date it never expires. Tokens stop working anyway once the user
loses TAK access.

permanentAccounts.description:
Accounts created for this event (new members, synchronized participants) are permanent instead
of event accounts that are deleted when the event is archived.

meshtasticEnabled.description:
The event provisions Meshtastic radios. When off, profiles carry no Meshtastic part, radio
downloads are unavailable and channels and radio settings stay stored but unused. Like other
configuration it reaches participants of an active event with the next published revision.

timeZone.description: IANA time-zone identifier. Fixed offsets such as `+01:00` are rejected.

startsAt.description: Descriptive start instant; it never changes the lifecycle state.

endsAt.description: Descriptive end instant; it never changes the lifecycle state.

takLoginTokenDays.description:
Days a TAK login token (QR code or typed instead of the password) stays valid. `0` keeps it valid
until the event's end date, or with no end date it never expires. Defaults to `0`. Tokens stop working anyway once the user
loses TAK access.

permanentAccounts.description:
Accounts created for this event (new members, synchronized participants) are permanent instead
of event accounts that are deleted when the event is archived. Defaults to `false`.

meshtasticEnabled.description: The event provisions Meshtastic radios. Defaults to `false`, a TAK-only event.

takLoginTokenDays.description:
Days a TAK login token (QR code or typed instead of the password) stays valid. `0` keeps it valid
until the event's end date, or with no end date it never expires. Omitted keeps the current value. Tokens stop working anyway once the user
loses TAK access.

permanentAccounts.description:
Accounts created for this event (new members, synchronized participants) are permanent instead
of event accounts that are deleted when the event is archived. Omitted keeps the current value.

meshtasticEnabled.description: The event provisions Meshtastic radios. Omitted keeps the current value.

accounts.description: Event accounts of the event that are now permanent.

slug.description: Stable key used by integrations, unique within the event, e.g. `participant`.

takRoleOverride.description:
ATAK role for members of this role, replacing their event group's default TAK role, e.g.
`Team Lead` for platoon leaders. `null` keeps the group's role.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

takRoleOverride.description: Omit to keep the current override; `null` removes it.

occurrences.description: How often the integration reported this unresolved member.

username.description: Name reported by the integration for this event.

callsign.description: Effective callsign, unique within the event; also the Meshtastic long name.

callsignOverride.description: Administrator override replacing the group's callsign format for this member.

shortName.description: Meshtastic short name such as `B1`; `null` while the group has no short-name prefix.

enrolledTakApps.description:
TAK apps the member's user has enrolled with the built-in TAK server and that may still
connect (valid client certificates). Certificates belong to the user, not to one event.

ExternalMemberSyncResult.description: Either the resolved membership or the recorded sync issue; never a credential or session.

callsignOverride.description: Callsign to use instead of the group format, e.g. to resolve a callsign conflict.

memberIds.description: Every member of the group exactly once, in the new short-name order (first becomes 1).

notifyMembers.description:
Emails members whose short name changed, if they have a confirmed address, asking them to set
up their radio again. Otherwise the change is only shown to the administrator.

ExternalProvider.description: Opaque lowercase namespace of the external system, e.g. `discord`. It is not a login provider.

ExternalId.description: Identifier of the person inside the external system, e.g. a Discord user ID.

username.description: Name reported by the external system; used for display and callsigns.

eventRole.description: Slug of an existing event role.

group.description: Slug of an existing event group.

userId.description: Existing OpenMeshTak user; their display name feeds the group's callsign format.

callsignOverride.description: Callsign to use instead of the group format.
Callsign to use instead of the group format.

displayName.description: Name of the new person; it feeds the group's callsign format.

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name; derived from the display name when omitted.

callsignOverride.description: Callsign to use instead of the group format; `null` returns to the group format.

ProvisioningName.description: Identifier used for TAK server groups.

callsignFormat.description:
Callsign template. Allowed placeholders: `{username}` (required) and `{group}`.
Example: `{username} [Bravo]`.

shortNamePrefix.description:
Meshtastic short-name prefix, e.g. `B` for `B1`, `B2`. Unique within the event.
`null` until chosen; activation requires it.

serverGroups.description:
Group names for an external TAK server, passed on unchanged in each member's profile for
integrations. The built-in TAK server ignores them; the event alone decides who sees whom.

slug.description: Stable key used by integrations, unique within the event, e.g. `bravo`.

provisioning.description: Callsign, TAK and short-name settings shared by every member of the group.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

provisioning.description: Optional; defaults to the plain username, Cyan, Team Member and the first slug letter.
Complete replacement of the provisioning settings.

takRoleOverride.description: `null` when the role keeps the group's TAK role, and in revisions before version 5.

SnapshotChannel.description:
A channel's published settings. Keys never enter snapshots: they stay encrypted on the channel,
and rotation and release act on the channel directly so a leaked key stops being handed out at
once. `pskVersion` records which key was current when the revision was created.

SnapshotMeshtastic.description:
The event's Meshtastic firmware target and settings, with the profile file hash so an artifact
can always be traced back to the exact field definitions used to generate it.

SnapshotTak.description:
The Meshtastic app's TAK mesh channel; `null` in revisions created before version 4. Revisions
before version 6 also stored a connection mode, which the switch `meshtasticEnabled` replaced.

ConfigurationSnapshot.description:
Bump `schemaVersion` whenever the snapshot shape changes; old revisions are never rewritten.
Version 2 added `channels` in device order, the first being the primary channel; version 3
added `meshtastic`; version 4 added `tak`; version 5 added role TAK overrides; version 6 added
`meshtasticEnabled`.

meshtasticEnabled.description:
Whether the event provisions Meshtastic radios; `true` in revisions before version 6. When
`false`, `channels` is empty and `meshtastic` is `null`.

created.description: `false` when the configuration was unchanged and the latest revision is returned instead.

EmailSettingsDto.description: SMTP settings without the password, which is write-only.

passwordSet.description: Whether a password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

password.description: Omit to keep the stored password, `null` to remove it.

DownloadGrantDto.description: A link that downloads the artifact without a session, e.g. from a QR code on another device.

url.description: Treat as a secret: whoever has it can download the file until it expires.

number.description: Increments per data package, starting at 1.

snapshotHash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical snapshot, for provenance.

Position.description: GeoJSON position: `[longitude, latitude]` or `[longitude, latitude, altitudeMetresHae]`.

coordinates.description: Outer ring first, then holes; every ring repeats its first position at the end.

CircleGeometry.description:
A true circle, which GeoJSON cannot express: centre plus radius in metres. It is never stored as
a silently approximated polygon and maps to ATAK `u-d-c-c` circles.

PackageGeometry.description: RFC 7946 geometry in WGS84, plus circles as an explicit domain extension.

color.description: Marker, line and polygon outline colour.

strokeWidth.description: Line and outline width in pixels.

fillOpacity.description: Polygon fill opacity; the fill uses `color`.

CotType.description:
CoT event type, e.g. `b-m-p-s-m` (spot marker) or `a-f-G-U-C-I` (MIL-STD-2525 friendly
infantry).

TakMarker.description: Optional TAK presentation of a marker, kept so ATAK packages round-trip without loss.

cotType.description: Defaults to the spot marker `b-m-p-s-m`; `a-*` types are drawn as military symbols.

iconsetPath.description:
ATAK icon set path such as `COT_MAPPING_SPOTMAP/b-m-p-s-m/-35072` or an icon in a custom
icon set. Passed through unchanged; the editor shows a plain marker when it cannot draw it.

metadata.description: Rubber-sheet placement and similar display data; absent for plain files.

PackageSnapshot.description: Everything a package generator needs; timestamps and versions are left out on purpose.

contents.description: Missing only on schema-1 revisions created before package content existed.

number.description: Increments per data package, starting at 1.

snapshotHash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical snapshot, for provenance.

created.description: `false` when the draft equals the latest revision, which is returned instead.

offlineMaps.description: Offline map caches, including nested map packages.

PackageAudience.description:
Who receives the published Data Package: every event member, or only those matching any
selected group, role or member. The selection is ignored while `allMembers` is true.

PackageTakDelivery.description: When the built-in TAK server installs the package on members' TAK apps by itself.

onEnrollment.description: Right after a member enrolls a TAK app.

onConnection.description: Whenever a member's TAK app connects, if a newer revision exists.

latestRevision.description: Number of the newest published revision, or `null` while nothing is published.

latestRevisionSize.description:
Approximate download size in bytes of the newest revision's ATAK Data Package, or `null`
while nothing is published. Counts attached files plus uncompressed CoT.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: `true` when publishing would create a new revision: nothing is published yet or the draft differs.

draftContents.description: What the draft holds, by kind.

sources.description: Published package revisions whose content was copied into this package's initial draft.

sortOrder.description: Drawing order within the event; lower values are drawn first, below higher ones.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

packageIds.description: Every data package of the event, bottom first; the last one is drawn on top.

tak.description: Only markers carry TAK metadata; `null` means a plain spot marker.

style.description: Defaults to a blue outline with a light fill.

layerId.description: Moving an object to another layer of the same data package is allowed.

tak.description: Markers only; send `null` for a plain spot marker.

feature.description: Which input feature this is about, e.g. `Feature 3 (Rally point)`.

ImportReport.description: Outcome of a GeoJSON or ATAK import; every input item appears somewhere in it.

changed.description: Imported, but adjusted: split multi-geometries, clamped styles.

retained.description: Opaque package files retained byte-for-byte, such as offline map caches.

skipped.description: Not imported because the content type is not supported, e.g. GeometryCollection.

rejected.description: Not imported because the content is invalid, e.g. a self-intersecting polygon.

sortOrder.description: Drawing and export order; lower values are drawn first.

visible.description: Editor display only; hidden layers are still published.

locked.description: Locked layers reject object changes until they are unlocked.

GeoJsonDocument.description: Untrusted GeoJSON document: a FeatureCollection, a Feature or a bare geometry.

GeoJsonFeatureCollection.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection exported from a data package draft or revision.

revision.description: Published revision to use; omit for the newest one.

layerIds.description: Only these layers of the package; omit for all layers.

packages.description: Published package revisions and optional layer selections to copy.

corners.description:
Lower left, lower right, upper right and upper left corner as [longitude, latitude] in
WGS84, as ATAK placed the image.

bounds.description: West, south, east, north in WGS84 degrees.

PackageContentDto.description: Map content kept from an imported ATAK Data Package; exported unchanged with its layer.

size.description: Size of the stored file in bytes.

rubberSheet.description: Placement for display; only for rubber sheets.

offlineMap.description: Tile range for display; only for offline maps that could be read.

visible.description: Editor display only; the exported file is always unchanged.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

layerId.description: Moves the content to another layer of the same package.

reason.description: `not-published`: the package has no published revision yet.

CombinedExportNameClash.description: An object name used in more than one included package; both objects are kept.

name.description: Name of the combined Data Package; defaults to the event name.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version; send it back unchanged with updates.

status.description: Disabling an account immediately invalidates all of its API keys.

permissions.description: Complete replacement of the account's grants.

displayPrefix.description: Recognizable, non-secret beginning of the key.

key.description: Complete bearer value. It is returned exactly once and cannot be retrieved again.

expiresAt.description: Optional expiry instant; must lie in the future.

username.description: Sign-in and TAK login name; keeps the one derived from the name when omitted.

apiClientBearer.description: API key of an API client. Never send it in a URL.

info.title: OpenMeshTak Core API
info.description: Authoritative API for OpenMeshTak provisioning and mission distribution.

get.description: Lists users ordered by creation time, oldest first. Requires instance-wide `users.read`.

parameters.description: Matches part of the display name or email.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Only permanent accounts or only event accounts.
parameters.name: accountType

post.description:
Creates a user without a password and returns a single-use setup link, valid for seven days.
The person opens it, signs in once and sets their own password. The new user has no
permissions until added to a user group or an event. Requires `users.create`.

put.description: Renames a user. Requires instance-wide `users.edit`.

post.description:
Disables a user: all sessions end, and sign-in, access links and TAK connections are refused.
Administrators cannot disable themselves. Requires `users.disable`.
Enables a disabled user again. Requires `users.disable`.

Emails the user a single-use password-reset link if their address is verified. Administrators
never see or set passwords. Requires `users.password-reset`.

409.description: The user can already sign in

post.description:
Issues a new single-use setup link for a user who has not set a password yet. Earlier links
of the user stop working. Requires `users.setup-links`.
Signs the user out everywhere. Requires `users.sign-out`.

Turns an event account into a permanent account that stays when its event is archived.
Permanent accounts are returned unchanged. Requires `users.read` and
`event-accounts.manage` for the account's event.

Exchanges a single-use setup link of an administrator-created user for a browser session, so
the person can set their first password. The token is sent in the body, never in the URL.
Every unusable link returns the same `401`.

get.description: Lists user groups ordered by creation time, oldest first. Requires `user-groups.read`.

post.description: Creates a group. Callers can only grant permissions they hold themselves.

409.description: Version conflict, slug conflict or protected system group

put.description: Replaces name, slug and grants. Requires the current `version`.

get.description: Lists the group's members ordered by user creation time, oldest first.

put.description:
Adds a user to the group. Idempotent. The caller must hold every grant of the group, because
membership passes those grants on.

409.description: Last member of a system group

delete.description: Removes a user from the group. A system group always keeps at least one member.

get.description: Requires `tak-traffic.view` for the event.

put.description: Turns recording on or off and sets the retention in days. Requires `events.manage`.

get.description:
The recorded positions and markers as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, oldest first, at most
50,000 items. Requires `tak-traffic.view`; every export is audited.

put.description: Replaces the settings. Requires the current `version` (0 before the first save).

Adds a publicly trusted server certificate for the TAK host name, e.g. the `fullchain.pem` and
`privkey.pem` of Let's Encrypt, so devices trust the server without the OpenMeshTak CA.
Requires a recent sign-in. Client certificates are still issued by the OpenMeshTak CA.

delete.description:
Removes an added, ACME or file certificate and disables ACME and the file reload; the server then uses one issued by the
OpenMeshTak CA.

put.description:
Uses the reverse proxy's certificate files, mounted read-only below `certificateDirectory`.
Core reloads them every twelve hours, so a certificate the proxy renews is picked up. Disables ACME.

get.description:
Connected TAK apps of the event and their current positions and markers, from the built-in
TAK server's memory. Requires `tak-traffic.view` for the event.

post.description:
Returns the TAK login of the signed-in user (account username, used with the account
password) and a fresh QR token in the ATAK enrollment link. The token lifetime of the user's
active events decides how long it is valid (`expiresAt`, `null` for no time limit). Members of
active events and holders of `tak-server.admin-access` may
enroll. QR tokens never carry the account password.

409.description: TAK server not enabled, or an earlier iTAK package certificate is still valid

get.description:
An iTAK connection package with the configured server ports, trust material and a newly
issued user-bound client identity. The private client key exists only in this download.
The 500 newest certificates.

post.description: Revokes a certificate; its TAK connections end immediately and it cannot reconnect.

get.description:
Lists the active CA and older CAs that are still trusted. A new installation creates its own
CA on the first call. Private keys are never returned.

post.description:
Generates a new CA and makes it the active one. The previous CA stays trusted until it
expires. Requires a recent sign-in.

Imports an existing CA and makes it the active one. The previous CA stays trusted until it
expires. Requires a recent sign-in; the key is encrypted at rest and never returned.

put.description: Replaces settings. The provider token is write-only; omit it to keep the stored value.

post.description: Immediately obtains or renews the public certificate with the configured solver.

Runs the saved settings against Let's Encrypt staging to check the setup without touching the
production rate limits. Nothing is installed; a failure is returned as `succeeded: false`.

put.description: Replaces the TAK connection settings. Requires the current `version` (0 before the first save).

get.description: Reports whether first-administrator setup has been completed. Reveals nothing else.

post.description: Creates the first password-backed administrator using the one-time operator token.

get.description:
Core's most recent log lines from memory, sanitized like the container log. Without `after`
it returns the newest lines; with `after` only lines written since. Requires instance-wide
`server-logs.read`.
Reports whether people may create their own account. Reveals nothing else.

post.description:
Creates an account and signs it in, if registration is open or invite-only with a usable
invite. New accounts have no permissions until an administrator grants some.

get.description: Who may create their own account. Requires `registration.manage`.

put.description: Closes registration, makes it invite-only or opens it to everyone. Requires `registration.manage`.

get.description: The 50 most recent registration invites, newest first. Requires `registration.manage`.

post.description:
Issues a single-use registration link, valid for seven days, for invite-only registration.
The link is returned once. Requires `registration.manage`.
Revokes an unused invite immediately. Requires `registration.manage`.

get.description:
Resolves the member's callsign, TAK and Meshtastic identity. Requires
`members.read`, being that member in an active event, or `member-artifacts.download` in an
active event, which is audited as an on-behalf view. Draft events return an administrator
preview of the unpublished configuration.
Lists the signed-in user's memberships in active events.

Delivers an audited Meshtastic channel URL to the signed-in member when the published event
configuration designates that member as a key holder. The URL contains secret key material.

Describes the authenticated caller and its effective grants. Integrations use it to verify
an API key; the Web application uses it to adapt navigation. It never replaces server-side
authorization.

Lists full releases, newest first. When the flasher cannot be reached, the last downloaded
list is returned; without one the list is unknown. Requires `events.manage` for at least one
event.
Whether Core looks up releases. Requires instance-wide `settings.manage`.

put.description: Switches release lookups on or off. Requires instance-wide `settings.manage`.

get.description: Lists the supported firmware lines, newest first.
Returns the sections, fields and enums of one profile.

put.description: Replaces the settings for the current firmware version. Requires the current `version`.

Sets or clears write-only secrets such as the Wi-Fi or MQTT password. Values are never
returned; `secretsSet` only says which secrets hold a value. Requires the current `version`.

post.description: Reports which settings a firmware change would keep, drop, invalidate or add.

409.description: Version conflict, unconfirmed change or event archived

put.description:
Changes the recommended firmware. Except for raising the minimum patch within a line, send
the `confirmation` of the preview that was accepted.

get.description: Lists the event's channels in creation order; sort by `sortOrder` for the device order.

409.description: Name in use, channel limit reached or event archived

post.description: Creates a channel; without `psk` the server generates a random 32-byte key.

409.description: Version conflict, name in use or event archived

put.description: Replaces everything except the key. Requires the current `version`.

post.description: Replaces the key, for example after a leak. Audited; requires the current `version`.

409.description: Version conflict, channel not withheld or event archived

post.description:
Releases a withheld secret channel to its whole audience. Audited; requires the current
`version`.
Returns the plain key. Requires `channel-keys.reveal`; every reveal is audited.

409.description: Meshtastic configuration not published or event without Meshtastic

get.description:
Generates the signed-in member's Meshtastic device profile (`.cfg`) from the published event
configuration: owner names, device role, the event's radio settings and the channels the
member receives now. An operator with `member-artifacts.download` receives exactly the
member's file on their behalf. The file contains channel keys; every download is audited. The file
name names the firmware line it is made for.
The member's packages; `members.read` previews and `member-artifacts.download` acts on their behalf.
Downloads the newest published revision as an ATAK Data Package, for the member or on their behalf.
Lists the member's 20 most recent claims without their tokens. Requires `members.read`.

post.description:
Issues a 24-hour single-use claim and returns its token exactly once. Earlier open claims of
the member are revoked. Requires `member-claims.create` and an active event.
Revokes an open claim immediately. Repeating the request is harmless.

403.description: The account has its own sign-in

post.description:
Exchanges a single-use participant claim for a normal browser session. The token is sent in
the body, never in the URL. Every unusable claim returns the same `401`.

get.description: The base map the Web app shows. Readable by every signed-in user.

put.description: Changes the base map for everyone. Requires instance-wide `settings.manage`.

get.description: How this installation presents itself. Public, because the sign-in page shows it.

put.description: Renames the installation. Requires instance-wide `settings.manage`.

get.description: Reports that the API process completed startup, including its database connection.
Lists the events the caller may read, ordered by creation time, oldest first.

parameters.description: Only return events in this lifecycle state.
parameters.name: status

409.description: Slug already in use; Idempotency-Key conflict

post.description: Creates a new event in the `draft` state. Requires instance-wide `events.manage`.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Version conflict, slug conflict or archived event

put.description:
Replaces the editable event settings. Requires the current `version`. The lifecycle state is
changed only through dedicated transitions, and archived events are read-only.

409.description: Version conflict, invalid transition or event not ready

post.description:
Moves a draft event to `active`. Requires `events.manage` and at least one event role and
one event group; unmet requirements are listed in the problem's `errors`.

Moves an active event to the read-only `archived` state. Requires `events.manage`. Its event
accounts are deleted with their sign-in, sessions and TAK certificates; accounts that are still
members of another unarchived event move to that event instead.

409.description: Version conflict, invalid transition or event not ready

post.description:
Returns an archived event to `active` after repeating activation validation. Requires
`events.reactivate`. Revoked or expired credentials, artifacts and download grants stay
invalid; clients regenerate what they need.

Turns every current event account of the event into a permanent account, so archiving no
longer deletes them. Requires `event-accounts.manage` for the event.

get.description: Lists the event's roles ordered by creation time, oldest first.

409.description: Slug already in use or event archived; Idempotency-Key conflict

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Version conflict, slug conflict or event archived

put.description: Replaces name, slug and description. Requires the current `version`.

409.description: Event archived or role still assigned to members

get.description: Lists synchronizations that could not be resolved, oldest first. Requires `members.read`.

parameters.description: Only return issues in this state.
parameters.name: status

200.description: Membership resolved or issue still open

409.description: Issue not open or event archived

post.description:
Re-evaluates an open issue against the event's current roles and groups. Requires
`members.manage`. A callsign override resolves a callsign conflict for this member.

409.description: Members changed meanwhile, short name too long or event archived

put.description:
Renumbers the group's short names `1..n` in the given order. Send every current member of
the group exactly once. Requires `members.manage`. Devices keep their old short name until
the member is provisioned again.

200.description: Membership resolved or sync issue recorded

put.description:
Idempotently creates or updates the event membership of an external identity. Requires
`members.sync` for the event. When the role or group slug does not exist, the response
contains a sync issue instead and nothing else changes. Synchronization never creates a
password, login, email address or session.

get.description: Lists the event's members ordered by creation time, oldest first. Requires `members.read`.

409.description: Already a member, callsign or short-name conflict, or event archived; Idempotency-Key conflict

post.description:
Adds an existing OpenMeshTak user to the event. Members from external systems use the
external-member upsert instead. Requires `members.manage`.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Username taken, callsign or short-name conflict, or event archived

post.description:
Creates a new person and adds them to the event in one step. Returns a single-use setup link,
valid for seven days, so they choose their own password. The account is an event account that
is deleted when the event is archived, unless the event keeps its accounts
(`permanentAccounts`). Requires `member-accounts.create`.

409.description: Version conflict, callsign or short-name conflict, or event archived

put.description:
Replaces the member's event role, event group and callsign override. Requires the current
`version` and `members.manage`. An integration sync may later set role and group again.

delete.description:
Removes the member from this event only. The user and other event participations remain.
Requires `members.manage`.

get.description: Lists the event's groups ordered by creation time, oldest first.

409.description: Slug already in use or event archived; Idempotency-Key conflict

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Version conflict, slug conflict or event archived

put.description: Replaces name, slug and description. Requires the current `version`.

409.description: Event archived or group still assigned to members

get.description: Lists revisions oldest first. Requires `events.read`.

post.description:
Publishes the current configuration of an active event. Returns the latest revision with
`created: false` when nothing changed. Requires `events.manage`.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

put.description: Replaces the settings. The SMTP password is write-only: omit it to keep the stored one.

post.description: Sends a test email with the stored settings.

409.description: An iTAK package certificate is still valid

post.description:
Creates a link that downloads one artifact the signed-in user may download right now, valid
for 5 minutes and at most 3 downloads. Access is checked again when the link is used.

404.description: Link invalid, used up or expired

get.description: Downloads the artifact of a download link without a session.
Lists published revisions, oldest first, without their snapshots.

200.description: Published, or the unchanged latest revision

post.description: Publishes the current draft. Requires `data-packages.publish`.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description: Returns one revision with its snapshot.

200.description: Data packages in their new order

409.description: Packages changed meanwhile or event archived

put.description: Replaces the order with the complete list of package IDs, bottom first.

get.description: Lists the data package's objects in creation order, optionally only those of one layer.

409.description: Layer locked, too many objects or event archived; Idempotency-Key conflict

422.description: Invalid geometry or other validation failure

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

409.description: Version conflict, layer locked or event archived

422.description: Invalid geometry or other validation failure

put.description: Replaces the object. Requires the current `version`.

409.description: Too many objects or event archived

post.description:
Creates a data package from an ATAK Data Package (`application/zip`) or a CoT file
(`application/xml`) and imports it into the first layer. The name comes from the package
manifest, otherwise from `fileName`. A failed import leaves no package behind.

get.description: Lists the data package's layers in creation order; sort by `sortOrder` for display.

409.description: Too many layers or event archived; Idempotency-Key conflict

post.description: Adds a layer on top of the existing ones.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

put.description: Replaces name, order, visibility and lock state. Requires the current `version`.

delete.description: Deletes the layer and all of its objects.

get.description: Exports the current draft as KML; `layerId` limits it to one layer. Circles become polygons.
Exports a published revision as KML; `layerId` limits it to one layer.

409.description: Layer locked, too many objects or event archived

post.description:
Imports a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, Feature or geometry into the layer. Points, lines and
polygons are supported; multi-geometries are split. The report lists every adjustment, every
skipped and every rejected feature. Request bodies are limited to 1 MB.

get.description:
Exports the current draft as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with simplestyle properties.
`layerId` limits the export to one layer.
Exports a published revision as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection; `layerId` limits it to one layer.

409.description: Event archived, nothing published or package limits exceeded; Idempotency-Key conflict

post.description: Copies selected published layers with new UUIDs and records their source revisions.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description: Offline maps, nested map packages and rubber sheets kept from imports.
One XYZ tile of an offline map for display on the map; `404` where the cache has no tile.
The image of a rubber sheet for display on the map.

409.description: Version conflict, layer locked or event archived

put.description:
Renames, moves to another layer, shows/hides or changes the opacity of map content in the
draft. Requires `data-packages.edit` and the current `version`.

delete.description: Removes map content from the draft; published revisions keep it. Requires `data-packages.edit`.

409.description: Layer locked, too many objects or event archived

post.description:
Imports an ATAK Data Package (`application/zip`, at most 10 MB) or a single CoT event
(`application/xml`) into the layer. Markers, freeform shapes, rectangles and circles are
supported; the report lists every adjusted, skipped and rejected item.

get.description:
Downloads a published revision as an ATAK Data Package (ZIP with `MANIFEST/manifest.xml`).
`layerId` exports only that layer, as its own package.
Lists the event's data packages ordered by creation time, oldest first.

post.description: Creates a data package with one empty layer.

parameters.description: Makes retries safe: a repeated request returns the original response.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

put.description: Replaces name and description. Requires the current `version`.

delete.description: Deletes the data package with its layers, objects and published revisions.

put.description:
Sets who receives the package's published revisions: all members or selected groups, roles
and members. Requires `data-packages.publish` and the current `version`.

Chooses whether the built-in TAK server installs the package by itself on enrollment and/or
on every connection. Requires `data-packages.publish` and the current `version`.

post.description: Reports which packages and revisions an export would include, skip or name twice.
Builds the combined ATAK Data Package. Audited with the exported revisions.

get.description: Lists API clients ordered by creation time, oldest first.

post.description: Creates an API client with explicit permission grants.

put.description: Replaces name, description, status and grants. Requires the current `version`.

get.description: Lists safe API-key metadata. Key secrets are never returned after creation.

post.description:
Creates an API key and returns its complete value exactly once. Creating a key while another
is active is a rotation. Requires a recent sign-in.
Revokes an API key immediately. Repeating the request is harmless.

409.description: Password already set or username taken

post.description:
Completes an account without a password, for example right after signing in with an access
link: optionally picks the username and sets the first password, used for sign-in and the TAK
login. Accounts that already have a password change it through the authentication API.
